newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares edging higher, seen in holding range.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares edging higher, seen in holding range.

text.p: Greek equities were slightly in the plus column in early trade with banks trading firmer and brokers expecting tight range trading and a gradual shift of interest from banks to industrial shares.
"The market is likely to hold around current levels as there is a gradual shift of interest from banks to industrials," said Telesis Securities.

Following a better-than-expected March CPI inflation figure -- 6.0 percent -- banks started a new round of interest rate cuts last week. The focus now is on April CPI which is expected to dip below 6.0 percent.
An informal Reuters poll of bankers and economists produced a mean forecast of 5.7 percent. Forecasts ranged from 5.5 - 6.0 percent.
Subscriptions to Xiosbank's IPO which started on Tuesday April 15 will end on Friday April 18. The bank is going public at 2,650 drachmas a share seeking to raise 4.43 billion.
The Athens general share index was trading 0.10 percent or 1.47 points higher at 1,414.89 from Wednesday's 1,413.42 close, after opening at 1,418.70.
Turnover was 4.47 billion drachmas. Decliners led advancers 100 to 76 with 23 issues unchanged on 199 traded.
Banks were up 0.52 percent with construction shedding 1.19 percent and industrials edging 0.24 percent higher.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas was quoted at 1,084.0-1,114.0. Shares of OTE telecom, the underlying, was 30 drachmas at 6,120.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $58.34-$60.04. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.
The ING Baring Financial Products American- style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 2,018-2,210 drachmas.
The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $12.18-$13.88. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
